newsitem.title: USA: PacifiCorp says project gets financing.
newsitem.headline: PacifiCorp says project gets financing.

text.p: PacifiCorp said Thursday that it and its partners, Aboitiz Equity Ventures Inc and Pacific Hydro Ltd, have secured financing for a hydro development project in the Philippines.
The amount of financing for the $145 million, 70 megawatt Bakun project was not disclosed. The project is on the Bakun River in the Cordillera Central mountain range in northern Luzon.
PacifiCorp's equity investment is about $15 million. Construction is under way and the project is expected to be completed by mid-2000.
"This is a stepping stone on the path to broader participation in the Philippine's energy sector," PacifiCorp Vice President Mike Henderson said in a statement.

"We intend to invest in additional generation projects as well as electric distribution opportunities as they are presented. We are impressed with the economic environment in the Philippines and are confident it will be a high growth market for electricity."

The Bakun Project involves an arrangement in which private companies build and operate facilities for periods up to 25 years, then transfer ownership to the National Power Corporation, a government-owned generation and transmission company.

In exchange, the project receives the full backing of the Philippine government, and all electricity generated is sold to the NPC on a take-or-pay basis, which guarantees payment for all electricity available in U.S. dollars.
